item.title: China's Zheng Qinwen reaches China Open semifinals
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Zheng Qinwen of China hits a return during the women's singles quarterfinal match between Zheng Qinwen of China and Elina Svitolina of Ukraine at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 9, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Han) BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- China's Zheng Qinwen advanced to the women's singles semifinals of the China Open here on Friday, defeating sixth seed Elina Svitolina of Ukraine 6-3, 7-6(6) on her first day after turning 24. Playing her first top-10 opponent of the tournament, wildcard Zheng broke serve three times in the opening set. She claimed breaks in the first and seventh games, only to be broken herself while serving for the set at 5-3, before securing her third break in the ninth game to close it out 6-3. Svitolina raised her level in the second set and broke Zheng in the seventh game to move 4-3 ahead, only for the Chinese to hit back immediately in the eighth. Both players held serve to force a tie-break, where Zheng trailed 0-2 before winning four straight points to lead 4-2. Svitolina drew level at 6-6, but Zheng sealed the win on her second match point at 8-6. "She performed excellently in the second set. That tie-break was really so close. Both of us played at a really high level. Honestly speaking, I really wanted to win this match, so I felt nervous when I hit the balls," Zheng said. Zheng, who spent her 24th birthday on Thursday, said, "I hope at 24 I can become more mature, and stay calm facing every single point on court. That is my own expectation for myself," she said. The result sends Zheng into her second China Open semifinal, matching her best run at the event, and her first WTA 1000 semifinal this year. ■ Zheng Qinwen of China hits a return during the women's singles quarterfinal match between Zheng Qinwen of China and Elina Svitolina of Ukraine at 2026 China Open tennis tournament in Beijing, China, Oct. 9, 2026. item.title: Column: China's quiet rise in global appeal
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
by Nadeem Javaid Over more than a decade of travelling across China, I have watched a transformation that is difficult to capture in economic statistics alone. Since 2013, each visit has revealed not simply a richer or more modern China, but a country steadily changing the way it produces, innovates, consumes and, increasingly, how it is perceived by the world. What strikes me most today is not simply how much China has changed. It is how the nature of that change has evolved. Perhaps one phrase captures this journey best: from "Made in China" to "Designed in China." For decades, much of the world encountered China through the products it manufactured -- a symbol of extraordinary scale and efficiency. But the China I see today is different. It is increasingly a China of electric vehicles, batteries, renewable energy, artificial intelligence, robotics and sophisticated consumer products. Chinese companies no longer compete only on cost and scale, but increasingly on technology, design, quality and consumer experience. This is more than industrial transformation. It is reputational transformation. During a recent visit to Urumqi, the capital of northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, I experienced a demonstration of autonomous driving technology at the airport. What struck me was not simply the technology itself, but how naturally such innovation seemed to fit into everyday life. It was a small but telling experience: technologies once associated with the future are increasingly becoming part of the present in China. The journey from "Made in China" to "Designed in China" is becoming visible to consumers. Yet some of the most revealing changes I have observed since 2013 are not inside factories or technology parks. They are in everyday life. China's cities today offer a dramatically different consumer experience. Coffee shops and cafés have become woven into urban culture. Domestic brands have grown more confident and sophisticated. Digital payments have transformed daily transactions. What may appear to be small changes tell us something important: development is ultimately reflected in people's everyday lives, and greater choice is perhaps one of the least discussed dividends of growth. In many interactions, I repeatedly heard an idea that initially sounded unconventional -- the application of market principles within socialism with Chinese characteristics. Yet China found ways to combine market incentives, entrepreneurship and competition with long-term state guidance and national priorities. What appeared contradictory in theory proved remarkably workable in practice. What mattered was the willingness to experiment, learn, adapt and scale what worked. From the establishment of the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone to today's advances in batteries, electric vehicles and renewable technologies, China's experience shows that institutions and policies must evolve as the economy evolves. This matters greatly for the developing world. Much of traditional development discourse focuses on managing vulnerability: poverty, debt and institutional weaknesses. These are real challenges. But developing societies do not only want to manage scarcity. They also want to create prosperity. They ask how to build productive firms, competitive industries and technological capabilities; how to move from imitation to innovation; and how to climb the global value chain. China's experience speaks directly to these aspirations -- not as a template to copy, but as evidence that transformation at scale is possible. Pakistan provides a concrete lens. Through years of working on economic policy and observing China-Pakistan cooperation, I have seen how perceptions change when bilateral ties become tangible to people. The upgrades to the Karakoram Highway, which have reduced travel times between remote regions; energy projects that have eased chronic power shortages; and affordable technology and educational exchanges all speak more powerfully than diplomatic statements ever could. Of course, China's experience is neither flawless nor simply transplantable. Every country has its own history, institutions and political economy. But when cooperation translates into lived experiences, those experiences gradually shape a country's reputation. Perhaps this helps explain why China is increasingly viewed in a more positive light around the world. People are not simply hearing about China anymore. Increasingly, they are experiencing China -- through its technologies, products, brands, infrastructure, universities and, for millions of visitors, through direct experience of China itself. A country once known mainly for producing what the world designed is increasingly designing what the world wants to use. Reputation is rarely built by slogans. It is built through experience. And the most enduring influence may be the one people can see, use and remember. Editor's note: Nadeem Javaid is the vice chancellor of the Pakistan Institute of Development Economics and a member of the Planning Commission of Pakistan. The views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the positions of Xinhua News Agency.■

item.title: Flame for Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade lit in Turin
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
Mayor of Changchun Gu Gang (2nd L) and president of FISU Leonz Eder (1st L) jointly light the cauldron with the torch from the first World University Games in Turin in 1959 during the flame collection ceremony for the Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade in Turin, Italy, Oct. 8, 2026. (Xinhua/Wang Kaiyan) TURIN, Italy, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- The flame for the Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade was lit Thursday in Turin, Italy, where the first World University Games were held in 1959, beginning its journey to China ahead of the January event. Changchun Mayor Gu Gang and International University Sports Federation President Leonz Eder jointly lit a cauldron using a torch from the inaugural Games before transferring the flame to a lantern for the Changchun Games. The lantern was carried through central Turin from the University of Turin to the Polytechnic University of Turin, passing the Egyptian Museum along the way. Gu expressed hope that the flame would symbolize friendship and that winter sports would promote cultural exchanges between East and West, fostering mutual understanding among young people worldwide. A welcoming ceremony for the flame is scheduled for October 14 in Changchun, according to the Games' organizing committee. The Winter Universiade will run from January 15 to 25, 2027. Eder recently told Xinhua that preparations were progressing smoothly and expressed confidence that the Games would attract a record number of participating delegations. ■ The cauldron is lit during the flame collection ceremony for the Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade in Turin, Italy, Oct. 8, 2026. item.title: China warns Philippines to cease provocations, false claims
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 8 (Xinhua) -- The China Coast Guard (CCG) on Thursday warned the Philippine side to immediately stop its infringements, provocations and false claims after a Philippine Coast Guard vessel transported an injured person from a grounded vessel near Ren'ai Jiao. Jiang Lue, a spokesperson for the CCG, said that on Thursday, Philippine Coast Guard vessel 4409 went to waters near Ren'ai Jiao to transport one injured person from the vessel illegally grounded there. Out of humanitarian considerations, the Chinese side immediately allowed the Philippine side to transfer the injured person by small boat, and the CCG handled the matter in accordance with the law and regulations, and provided necessary assistance, Jiang said. The Philippine side's relevant remarks disregard the facts and distort the truth in an attempt to mislead the public, Jiang added. China has indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha Qundao, including Ren'ai Jiao, and the adjacent waters, he noted. ■

item.title: Chinese envoy blasts U.S. obsession with absolute strategic advantages at UNGA
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
UNITED NATIONS, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- U.S. obsession with "absolute strategic advantages" stalls the multilateral arms control process and erodes the international non-proliferation system, a Chinese envoy said Thursday at the UN General Assembly (UNGA). The United States is "obsessed with absolute strategic advantages," invests heavily every year in upgrading nuclear forces, promotes the Golden Dome anti-missile system, forward-deploys strategic offensive and defensive forces against other nuclear-armed countries, and continues to build nuclear alliances through "nuclear sharing and extended deterrence," said Sun Xiaobo, head of the Chinese delegation to the 81st session of the UNGA Disarmament and International Security Committee. Sun, director-general of the Arms Control Department of the Chinese Foreign Ministry, warned at the Committee's general debate that the negative acts of the United States seriously undermined global and regional strategic stability, as well as the security interests of other states, and raised the risk of nuclear confrontation and conflicts. The United States applies double standards on arms control and non-proliferation, adopts a utilitarian attitude toward the current multilateral arms control mechanism and treaty system, and has repeatedly withdrawn from treaties and organizations, he said. "This is the fundamental cause for the stalemate of the multilateral arms control process and the erosion of the international non-proliferation system," Sun said. China advocates that all states should practice true multilateralism, he noted. Calling the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons the cornerstone of the international nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament regime and an essential pillar of the post-war international security architecture, Sun said the consensus on the prohibition of nuclear tests based on the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty cannot be challenged. ■

item.title: China records 826 mln domestic tourist trips during 2026 National Day holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- China recorded 826 million domestic tourist trips during the seven-day National Day holiday, with tourism spending totaling 738.38 billion yuan (about 109.67 billion U.S. dollars), the Ministry of Culture and Tourism said Friday. On a daily average basis, the number of domestic trips rose 6.3 percent from the eight-day National Day and Mid-Autumn Festival holiday in 2025, while tourism spending increased 4.3 percent, according to the ministry. ■

item.title: Symposium held to study Xi's works on culture
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-09
BEIJING, Oct. 9 (Xinhua) -- A symposium was held in Beijing on Friday to study the first and second volumes of selected works on culture by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, attended the symposium and delivered a speech. The volumes were published in August by the Central Party Literature Press. Attendees at the symposium said the selections systematically present the fundamental principles, core content and essential requirements of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture, providing an authoritative textbook for its study and application. In studying the selections, it is important to consciously study and apply Xi Jinping Thought on Culture and better fulfill the cultural mission of the new era, they said. The attendees called for efforts to gain a deeper understanding of Xi Jinping Thought on Culture as the fundamental guidelines for public communication and cultural work in the new era, as well as its strategic vision for building China into a leading country in culture. They also urged efforts to translate the gains from studying it into concrete actions. Organized by the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, the symposium was attended by officials from relevant central departments, central publicity and cultural institutions, and publicity departments of provincial-level CPC committees, as well as experts and scholars in social sciences. The volumes of the selected works contain 78 pieces of the most important and fundamental works by Xi on cultural development from November 2012 to February 2026, featuring reports, speeches, letters and instructions. Xi Jinping Thought on Culture was formally put forward at a national meeting on the work of public communication and culture in October 2023. ■
